subject: Volume breakpoints, model premiums, and committed-tier proposal
messages:
From: Sara Milton <sara@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:32:00 -0500
Subject: Pricing question — breakpoints & premiums for hosted API

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers looked promising. Before we put together an internal business case, procurement asked me to get a clear picture of how Redwood structures volume discounts and how model-specific "premiums" are applied. A few specific asks: 

- We expect ~25M generated tokens/month (chat) + ~2M embedding units/month to start; please show example pricing at 25M, 75M, and 250M monthly usage.
- Do discounts apply per-token (flat price per token that decreases at breakpoints) or as a blended discount on the overall bill?
- Are premium models (you demoed "R-Prime-XL") treated as a per-token surcharge, a multiplier on the base price, or priced as separate SKUs?
- For committed tiers: do unused committed tokens roll over month-to-month or are they forfeited? Any flexibility for an initial ramp/credit?

If easier, a simple sample invoice or a spreadsheet with the scenarios above would be great. Procurement is also interested in whether embeddings are billed differently (per-embedding unit vs per-token).

Can you loop in whoever owns pricing? We're hoping to finalize vendor shortlist by Dec 1.

Best,
Sara Milton
Head of Cloud Platform
Nimbus Analytics

---
Attachment: (none)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Milton <sara@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:11:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pricing question — breakpoints & premiums for hosted API

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Looping Vanessa (AE) and including a short matrix below; attaching a spreadsheet (Nimbus_proposal_v1.xlsx) with line-item examples for the scenarios you listed.

Quick summary (ballpark net list before any negotiated commit credits):
- Baseline (standard chat model): $0.0009 per generated token at <10M/mo.
- Volume breakpoints (per-token pricing, not blended):
  * 10M–49.99M: $0.00072/token (20% off baseline)
  * 50M–199.99M: $0.00054/token (40% off baseline)
  * 200M+: $0.00045/token (50% off baseline)
- Premium models (e.g., R-Prime-XL): applied as an additive surcharge per token in this proposal, not a multiplier — currently +$0.0006/token over the chosen base model price. We price premium models as separate SKUs so customers can mix models in the same account and get accurate billing per call.
- Embeddings: billed as embedding units with a different baseline (example: $0.0018 per 1k embedding units at list; tiered discounts follow a separate breakpoint schedule).
- Committed tiers: commitments give a committed unit price and an upfront credit schedule. Unused committed tokens do not automatically roll over month-to-month, but we can structure a 3-month ramp window where unused commitment in month 1 can be applied to month 2 within the ramp period.

Notes and next steps:
- The spreadsheet shows your three scenarios (25M, 75M, 250M) with blended monthly cost examples assuming model mix: 90% standard chat + 10% R-Prime-XL + 2M embedding units.
- We can offer a one-time promotional credit to cover the initial integration costs (we typically do this for first-year committed agreements).
- SLA credits and enterprise support are added line items for Dedicated / Private deployments; for Hosted API we have a standard 99.95% target and credits are available on qualified incidents.

Vanessa — can you confirm whether a 60-day evaluation commit (50% of anticipated first-month usage as a refundable credit) is something we want to propose to Nimbus?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales — Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Nimbus_proposal_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 98KB)

Thanks for the draft, Jonas — a couple of adjustments I recommend before we send a formal quote to procurement:

1) Breakpoints — shift the middle bracket to 30M–149.99M and the top starts at 150M to keep bands more typical for mid-market customers. That gives better step-savings for Nimbus given their anticipated ramp.
2) Premium model pricing — we should present both options: (A) additive surcharge (your current proposal) and (B) a fixed premium SKU price so the buyer can compare. The spreadsheet should contain both columns.
3) Commit wording — clarify treatment of unused tokens: we can allow one-time rollover within the first 3 months if they opt into a 12-month commit.

I'd also propose an initial blended introductory rate for the first 90 days for the R-Prime-XL usage (cap at 10% of monthly consumption) to reduce friction during evaluation.

Vanessa — please confirm whether we can include a standard procurement SLA note and open a DocuSign envelope once Sara confirms the preferred pricing flavor.

Laura Bennett
Director, Pricing Strategy
Redwood Inference
